deviations.spec_said: Cover 'writes nothing when the release row and its joins cannot all be written' by driving createWithVersions with a non-existent version id and asserting no package_releases row was created; leave the case out and say so if pg-mem cannot support the assertion honestly.
deviations.did: Kept the case as 'when a pinned version does not exist > refuses the release', asserting only the rejection, with a comment in the spec explaining why the row-absence assertion is absent. createWithVersions still does all four inserts inside this.repository.manager.transaction(...).
deviations.why: pg-mem enforces the join-table foreign key (the write does reject), but its pg adapter treats ROLLBACK as a no-op - verified standalone: an insert inside BEGIN survives an explicit ROLLBACK, and the first run of the test showed the release row plus the command/standard join rows persisting. A 'leaves no release row behind' assertion could therefore never be honest in this harness.

deviations.spec_said: If this repository already has an established helper type for timestamp fields that sibling types use, prefer it over the two optional Date fields.
deviations.did: Kept the verbatim createdAt?: Date; updatedAt?: Date; fields.
deviations.why: No sibling type in packages/types/src/deployments uses WithTimestamps (Distribution and PackagesDeployment declare createdAt: string; the deployments schemas apply WithTimestamps at the EntitySchema level only). WithTimestamps would also make createdAt/updatedAt required on the createWithVersions input, forcing callers to invent DB-generated values.
